hero.headline: Trump considers government stake in top AI companies
hero.teaser: The Trump administration is exploring taking equity positions in leading artificial intelligence firms, with meetings planned as soon as next week.
hero.body:
President Trump said his administration is considering taking government ownership stakes in top artificial intelligence companies. The discussions include possible government equity in OpenAI, with talks already underway about the arrangement.

Trump indicated he may meet with artificial intelligence companies as soon as next week to discuss a government profit-sharing plan. The proposal would give the federal government partial ownership in exchange for supporting AI development, representing a significant departure from traditional government-industry relationships in the technology sector.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes in Gulf as ceasefire frays
cards.body:
The United States and Iran engaged in direct military strikes on Thursday in the most serious challenge yet to their month-long ceasefire agreement. The exchange raised questions about whether the fragile truce could survive further escalations.

The US military said it targeted Iranian military facilities after Iranian forces launched multiple missiles, drones and small boats at three American destroyers transiting the Strait of Hormuz. The Pentagon stated that no US assets were struck and that its forces eliminated the inbound threats while targeting Iranian missile and drone launch sites, command centers, and surveillance nodes.

Iran disputed the American account, accusing the US of violating the ceasefire by targeting two ships at the strait and conducting airstrikes on civilian areas along the Iranian coast, including the island of Qeshm, which is home to approximately 150,000 people. Iran's military said it responded by attacking US military vessels, claiming to have inflicted significant damage on them.

The United Arab Emirates reported intercepting Iranian missiles and drones hours after the strikes. Brent crude oil prices rose to around $101 per barrel following news of the attacks.

President Trump described the incident as a minor affair, calling it a "love tap" during an interview with ABC News. "They trifled with us today," Trump told reporters. "We blew them away." He insisted the ceasefire remained intact despite the strikes.

When asked about prospects for a broader negotiated settlement, Trump said a deal "might not happen, but it could happen any day." He claimed Iran wanted an agreement more than the United States did.

The confrontation comes as reports suggested the two countries may have been close to a temporary agreement to halt the conflict. A one-page memorandum was reportedly shared between Washington and Tehran through Pakistan. However, senior Iranian officials have recently rejected concessions, with some preferring to delay negotiations until closer to the November midterm elections in the US, when the Trump administration might face pressure to reach a settlement.

Regional diplomats warned that Iran could miscalculate. They suggested the current moment offered an opportunity to end the conflict and claim victory, which might become harder if large-scale fighting resumes. They also noted that if negotiations failed, Washington could unilaterally end the conflict and leave Iran facing severe economic sanctions.

The strikes occurred in and around the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz, through which a significant portion of global oil shipments pass. The US has been pressuring Iran to reopen the strait and has enforced a naval blockade of Iranian ports. Earlier this week, Trump sent warships to guide stranded tankers through the waterway in an operation he called "Project Freedom."

Neither government has announced casualties from the strikes.

cards.headline: UN Security Council calls emergency session after Russian missile attack on Ukraine
cards.teaser: The Security Council will convene in response to what Ukraine described as ballistic missile terror by Russia.
cards.body:
The United Nations Security Council scheduled an emergency session following a large-scale Russian missile attack on Ukraine. The Permanent Representative of Latvia to the United Nations announced the meeting would address maintenance of peace and security in Ukraine.

Ukraine characterized the Russian assault as ballistic missile terror. The attack prompted immediate international response, with the Security Council convening to discuss the escalation in hostilities between Russia and Ukraine.

cards.headline: Israel strikes southern Lebanon after ordering village evacuations
cards.teaser: Israeli forces attacked southern Lebanon after directing residents of nine villages to leave their homes.
cards.body:
Israel conducted military strikes in southern Lebanon following evacuation orders for nine villages in the region. The operations continue amid stalled ceasefire negotiations between Lebanon and Israel.

Hezbollah has rejected a proposed ceasefire deal agreed upon by Israel and Lebanon. A U.N. peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon during the ongoing conflict.

cards.headline: Nasdaq drops 4.2% in worst day since April 2025 as chip stocks tumble
cards.teaser: The Nasdaq Composite fell 4.2% on Friday, marking its worst single-day decline since April 2025, as investors fled chip stocks and technology shares.
cards.body:
The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 4.2% on Friday, its worst day since April 2025, as semiconductor and technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also suffered significant losses in what became the year's worst trading day for major U.S. indexes.

The sharp selloff reflected investor concerns about stretched valuations in technology stocks and shifting expectations around Federal Reserve interest rate policy. Higher borrowing costs typically hurt growth-focused tech companies that rely on future earnings to justify their valuations. The decline halted the recent momentum in artificial intelligence and chip stocks that had driven much of the market's gains.

cards.headline: Whistleblower says DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A whistleblower alleges that a proposed plan would have incorrectly designated millions of living people as deceased.
cards.body:
A whistleblower has come forward with allegations that a plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead in government records. The alleged plan was part of an immigration enforcement push, according to the whistleblower's claims.

The disclosure raises concerns about the accuracy of government data systems and the potential consequences for millions of people who could have been wrongly recorded as deceased. The whistleblower did not specify which agency or office within the government developed the plan or when it was proposed.

cards.headline: Canada bans Texas cattle imports after screwworm outbreak
cards.body:
Canada has banned imports of cattle from Texas following the discovery of a flesh-eating parasite in the state. The action came after a second infected calf was identified, prompting Texas to declare a state of disaster.

The New World screwworm fly, which had not been confirmed in the United States since 1966, was found in a calf in south Texas, roughly 50 miles from the Mexico border. The parasite's larvae feed on the blood and flesh of warm-blooded animals, causing severe damage and death if untreated. Female screwworm flies lay eggs in open wounds on livestock, and the larvae quickly consume blood and tissue once they hatch.

For more than a year, the US Department of Agriculture and Texas officials have warned livestock owners about the parasite advancing through Mexico. Despite efforts to contain it, including the release of billions of sterile flies, the screwworm has spread over 1,100 miles from southern Mexico into Texas.

Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller criticized the federal response in a statement, saying the USDA had missed an important component of its containment strategy. He called for the Trump administration to increase deployment of the screwworm adult suppression system, or Swass, which uses attractants, bait, and targeted insecticides to reduce adult screwworm populations before sterile fly releases complete the eradication effort.

Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins defended her agency's response, stating there is no threat of mass infestation and no reason to believe the parasite will become established in the country. She noted that the Texas case was the only confirmed detection in the state so far.

The screwworm was eradicated from the United States in the 1970s after causing tens of millions of dollars in losses. Officials are concerned about a resurgence at a time when beef prices have reached record highs. While the flies pose no direct threat to food safety, officials fear potential shortages if the parasite spreads among cattle and poultry populations.

In response to the outbreak, the USDA has partnered with the Army Corps of Engineers and private construction company Mortenson to build a new sterile fly production facility at Moore Airbase in Edinburg, Texas. This facility will help combat the spread of the parasite.

Texas is a major cattle-producing state, and the livestock industry represents a significant portion of its agricultural economy. The trade restrictions imposed by Canada and the outbreak itself pose potential economic losses for Texas ranchers. The state's disaster declaration allows for faster deployment of resources and personnel to affected areas as officials work to contain the infestation and determine how the parasite reentered the United States.

cards.body:

Hezbollah has rejected a proposed ceasefire deal agreed upon by Israel and Lebanon. A U.N. peacekeeper was killed and others wounded when they came under mortar fire in southeastern Lebanon during the ongoing conflict.

cards.headline: Armenia holds election as Russia pressures pro-Western government
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan seeks a third term despite declining popularity and Russian opposition to his government's orientation.
cards.body:
Armenia prepared for elections as incumbent Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan campaigned for a third term in office. Pashinyan faces falling domestic support while Russia increases pressure on his pro-Western government.

The election occurs at a time of geopolitical tension, with Russia seeking to influence the outcome against the current government's Western-leaning policies. Pashinyan's administration has navigated between competing international pressures while managing domestic challenges to its popularity.

cards.headline: Canada bans Texas cattle imports after screwworm outbreak
cards.teaser: The Canadian government imposed restrictions following identification of a second infected calf in Texas.
cards.body:
Canada has implemented a ban on cattle imports from Texas following an outbreak of flesh-eating screwworm in the US state. The action was triggered after a second infected calf was discovered in Texas.

Texas declared a state of disaster in response to the screwworm outbreak. The Canadian import ban is designed to prevent the parasite from crossing the border. Screwworms are parasitic fly larvae that infest and feed on the living tissue of warm-blooded animals.

cards.headline: Iran's football team receives US visas for World Cup
cards.teaser: Officials confirmed the Iranian squad can enter the United States just 10 days before their opening match.
cards.body:
The Iranian national football team has been granted visas to enter the United States for the World Cup. The approval comes just 10 days before Iran's opening match against New Zealand in Los Angeles.

The visa decision resolves uncertainty about whether Iran would be able to participate in matches held on US soil despite longstanding tensions between the two countries.

cards.headline: Israeli gunfire kills Palestinian baby in West Bank
cards.teaser: The Palestinian health ministry reported the infant's death as the Israeli military said it is reviewing the incident.
cards.body: A Palestinian baby was killed by Israeli gunfire in the West Bank on Friday, according to the Palestinian health ministry. The Israeli military acknowledged the incident and said it is under review, while expressing deep sorrow for any harm caused.

cards.headline: US and Iran exchange strikes in Gulf
cards.teaser: The US military struck Iranian drones and radar sites, prompting Iranian retaliation against American bases in Kuwait and Bahrain.
cards.body:
The US military struck Iranian drones and radar sites in the Gulf region. Iran responded by targeting US military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain, marking the latest escalation between the two nations.

This exchange represents a test of the fragile ceasefire between Washington and Tehran amid ongoing tensions in the region.

cards.headline: Democrat Xavier Becerra advances in California governor race
cards.teaser: Democrat Xavier Becerra has advanced to the general election in November after winning California's gubernatorial primary.
cards.body:
Former Health and Human Services Secretary Xavier Becerra won the top spot in California's primary election for governor. His victory marks a significant comeback in one of the state's most competitive races in recent years as he advances to the November general election.

Election officials continue counting ballots to determine Becerra's opponent. He will face either fellow Democrat Tom Steyer, an environmental activist and billionaire who supports progressive policies including universal healthcare, or Republican Steve Hilton, a former UK political operative and Fox News personality who received Donald Trump's endorsement.

cards.headline: Major oil companies skip Arctic refuge drilling auction
cards.teaser: Large oil firms showed limited interest in the Trump administration's auction of drilling leases in Alaska's Arctic National Wildlife Refuge.
cards.body:
The Trump administration's sale of oil drilling rights in the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge drew a tepid response from major energy companies. Few bids were submitted for the leases, despite the administration's push to open the protected area to fossil fuel extraction.

The refuge, often called ANWR, has been at the center of a decades-long debate over energy development versus conservation. The limited interest from major oil producers suggests the leases may not be economically attractive under current market conditions.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 lead over Spurs in NBA Finals
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs by one point to take a commanding lead in the championship series.
cards.body:
The Knicks defeated the Spurs by one point in Game 2, securing a 2-0 series lead. Karl-Anthony Towns was instrumental for New York on both offense and defense. The Knicks became just the third team to win the first two games of the NBA Finals on the road.

New York returns home with two wins away from capturing its first championship since 1973. The franchise and its fans have been waiting generations for another title, and the Knicks will host the remaining games at their home arena.

cards.headline: Man charged after stabbing leaves boy with amputated leg
cards.teaser: An 18-year-old man faces charges of wounding with intent and possessing a knife after a stabbing at Barry Island left a boy with severe injuries.
cards.body:
An 18-year-old has been charged following a stabbing incident at Barry Island that resulted in a boy having his leg amputated. The suspect is due to appear in court on charges of wounding with intent and knife possession.

The incident occurred at the Welsh seaside resort, a popular destination for families and tourists. The severity of the boy's injuries required surgical amputation of his leg.

cards.headline: British actor Anthony Head dies at 72
cards.teaser: Anthony Head, known for roles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Ted Lasso, has died from complications related to pneumonia.
cards.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He died from complications of pneumonia.

Head's career spanned decades, beginning with his appearances in 1980s Nescafe advertisements before gaining international fame through Buffy. He went on to appear in numerous television shows including Merlin, Little Britain, and most recently Ted Lasso. His death has prompted tributes from colleagues and fans.

cards.body:
The Nasdaq Composite tumbled 4.2% on Friday, its worst day since April 2025, as semiconductor and technology stocks came under heavy selling pressure. The S&P 500 and Dow Jones Industrial Average also suffered significant losses in what became the year's worst trading day for major U.S. indexes.

The sharp selloff reflected investor concerns about stretched valuations in technology stocks and shifting expectations around Federal Reserve interest rate policy. Higher borrowing costs typically hurt growth-focused tech companies that rely on future earnings to justify their valuations. The decline halted the recent momentum in artificial intelligence and chip stocks that had driven much of the market's gains.

cards.headline: Google agrees to pay SpaceX nearly $1 billion monthly in cloud computing deal
cards.teaser: Google will pay SpaceX $920 million per month for computing capacity at data centers operated by xAI.
cards.body:
Google reached an agreement to pay SpaceX $920 million monthly for access to AI computing capacity. The deal involves computing resources at xAI data centers, marking one of the largest cloud computing arrangements disclosed to date.

The agreement comes as SpaceX prepares for a public offering and follows a similar arrangement between SpaceX and Anthropic. The monthly payments will provide Google with significant AI processing power while giving SpaceX a major revenue stream from its data center infrastructure ahead of its IPO.

cards.headline: Anthropic urges global pause in AI development, warns of self-improvement risk
cards.teaser: The AI company called for the world to have the option to halt artificial intelligence progress, citing risks that humans could lose control.
cards.body:
Anthropic proposed a global pause in AI development, warning that self-improving artificial intelligence systems pose significant risks. The company said the world should have the ability to stop AI progress if necessary to prevent humans from losing control of the technology.

The call for a potential pause represents a notable shift from an AI company actively developing advanced systems. Anthropic's position adds to growing debate about AI safety and regulation, with the company flagging specific concerns about AI systems that can improve themselves without human intervention.

cards.headline: Bitcoin falls below $60,000 to lowest level since October 2024
cards.teaser: Bitcoin dropped below $60,000 as investors shifted focus to AI stocks and other investments, with Zcash plunging 37%.
cards.body:
Bitcoin has dropped below $60,000, marking its lowest point since October 2024. The decline reflects shifting investor sentiment away from cryptocurrencies toward other assets like AI stocks and major IPOs. Zcash experienced an even steeper fall, plummeting 37% during the same period.

The sell-off erased significant value from cryptocurrency positions and signals changing market dynamics. Analysts point to broader trends suggesting Bitcoin could continue declining as investors redirect capital toward alternative investment opportunities.

cards.headline: SpaceX and other mega IPOs may wait years to join S&P 500
cards.teaser: The index rejected SpaceX for inclusion, a decision that would also block OpenAI and Anthropic from joining after their public offerings.
cards.body:
The S&P 500 has rejected SpaceX's entry into the index despite its massive valuation and upcoming IPO. This decision would also prevent OpenAI and Anthropic from joining the benchmark index that tracks 500 leading U.S. publicly traded companies.

SpaceX currently operates at a significant loss, which appears to have kept it out. The index's gatekeepers have substantial influence over which companies gain inclusion, affecting billions in investment flows. Once SpaceX goes public and eventually qualifies for inclusion, passive fund investors tracking the index will be forced to buy its shares.

cards.headline: Elon Musk leads list of highest-paid chief executives
cards.teaser: Executive compensation is accelerating while rank-and-file workers lag behind, widening the pay gap in corporate America.
cards.body:
Elon Musk topped the list of highest-paid chief executives as executive compensation continues to grow faster than worker pay. The data shows an expanding gap between what top executives earn and what typical employees receive.

Executive pay packages have accelerated in recent years while wage growth for rank-and-file workers has remained comparatively modest. The widening disparity has drawn increased scrutiny from shareholders and policymakers examining income inequality within major corporations.

hero.headline: Reid Hoffman leaves Microsoft board to focus on AI drug discovery startup Manus
hero.teaser: Reid Hoffman stepped down from Microsoft's board after a decade to concentrate on his artificial intelligence drug discovery company.
hero.body:
Reid Hoffman has stepped down from Microsoft's board after a decade of service to focus on Manus, his AI-driven drug discovery startup. His time on the Microsoft board proved financially rewarding for the LinkedIn co-founder and venture capitalist.

The move represents a shift to what Hoffman calls "founder mode," allowing him to dedicate his attention to hands-on leadership of Manus rather than board governance responsibilities. The startup applies artificial intelligence to pharmaceutical research and development.

cards.headline: Baby botulism outbreak cause remains unknown as FDA investigation continues
cards.teaser: Federal regulators have not determined the source of a baby botulism outbreak as three involved companies dispute responsibility.
cards.body:
The Food and Drug Administration has not identified the cause of a baby botulism outbreak or developed prevention measures. The investigation involves three companies, each attributing responsibility to the others for the outbreak that affected infants.

Botulism is a rare but serious illness caused by toxins that attack the nervous system. In infants, the condition typically occurs when babies ingest bacterial spores that produce toxins in the intestinal tract. The FDA's ongoing investigation aims to trace the source of contamination and establish protocols to prevent future cases.

cards.headline: Final Fantasy VII Revelation announced to conclude remake trilogy in 2027
cards.teaser: Square Enix revealed Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the concluding chapter of the remake trilogy, set for spring 2027 release.
cards.body:
Square Enix officially revealed Final Fantasy VII Revelation, the final installment in its Final Fantasy VII remake trilogy. The game will launch in spring 2027 across multiple platforms: PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, and Nintendo Switch 2.

The announcement came during Summer Game Fest Live, where Square Enix debuted gameplay footage and story details showcasing how the trilogy will conclude. This marks one of the first confirmed titles for the Nintendo Switch 2.

cards.headline: Stellar Blade sequel Blood Rain announced with debut trailer
cards.teaser: Developer Shift Up revealed Stellar Blade: Blood Rain, a sequel to the action game starring a new protagonist named Evie.
cards.body:
Shift Up unveiled Stellar Blade: Blood Rain at Summer Game Fest 2026, revealing a sequel to the PlayStation 5 action title Stellar Blade. The announcement came with a debut trailer that introduced Evie as the game's protagonist and showcased its combat and visual design.

The sequel is currently in development at Shift Up. The original Stellar Blade's commercial success led the studio to greenlight this follow-up, which was among the notable announcements featured at Summer Game Fest.

cards.headline: Guild Wars 3 announced for PC and PlayStation 5 with fall 2027 beta
cards.teaser: ArenaNet unveiled Guild Wars 3 at Summer Game Fest, positioning it as a modern evolution of the MMORPG genre.
cards.body:
Guild Wars 3 was officially announced at Summer Game Fest 2026 for PC and PlayStation 5. Developer ArenaNet described the game as a modern evolution of the massively multiplayer online role-playing game genre, with a beta test planned for fall 2027.

The announcement addressed questions about the fate of Guild Wars 2, which will continue to receive support alongside the development of the new title. Guild Wars 3 represents a significant expansion of the franchise beyond its traditional PC platform, with the PlayStation 5 version marking the first console release for the series. ArenaNet released initial details about gameplay systems and the game's approach to MMORPG design.

cards.headline: Hitman Classic Trilogy remaster announced for 2027 release
cards.teaser: IO Interactive revealed remasters of the first three Hitman games, coming to Xbox and other platforms in 2027.
cards.body:
IO Interactive revealed the Hitman Classic Trilogy Remastered at its IOI Access event, set to arrive in 2027 on Xbox and other platforms. The collection will bring updated versions of the original three Hitman games to modern consoles with enhanced graphics and technical improvements.

The announcement also featured news about upcoming downloadable content for current Hitman titles, including collaboration content with Wiz Khalifa. The remaster aims to serve both longtime fans and new players interested in experiencing Agent 47's early missions.

cards.headline: Founders share venture capital horror stories on social media
cards.teaser: A viral conversation on X featured startup founders describing negative experiences with venture capital investors, with some naming specific firms.
cards.body:
A viral conversation on X this week featured startup founders publicly sharing negative experiences with venture capital investors. The stories described a range of problematic encounters, from unusual requests to behavior founders viewed as inappropriate or unprofessional during funding discussions.

In a departure from typical industry diplomacy, some founders named specific venture capital firms and investors while recounting their experiences. The thread sparked broader conversation about power imbalances in startup financing and the tensions that emerge during capital-raising negotiations.

hero.headline: NBA investigating Clippers over alleged Kawhi Leonard salary cap violations
hero.teaser: The league has interviewed Kawhi Leonard and his business adviser as part of a probe into claims the team circumvented salary cap rules.
hero.body:
The NBA has interviewed Los Angeles Clippers star Kawhi Leonard and his business adviser Dennis Robertson as part of an investigation into allegations the team violated salary cap rules to compensate Leonard.

The probe was initiated following claims made by journalist Pablo Torre, who alleged that Clippers owner Steve Ballmer employed Leonard through a non-existent role at one of his companies to circumvent NBA salary cap restrictions. Torre's reporting, which cited legal documents, suggested the arrangement was designed to provide Leonard with additional compensation beyond his standard contract.

According to Torre's investigation, Ballmer partially funded a tree-planting company called Aspiration. The company then entered into a $28 million agreement with KL2 Aspire, LLC, a business owned by Leonard. Torre reported finding no evidence that Leonard performed any work for Aspiration. The contract between the two entities contained a clause that would allow Leonard to receive payment even if he did not work, and another clause voiding the deal if Leonard left the Clippers.

A former Aspiration employee told Torre the arrangement was designed to "circumvent the salary cap."

The Clippers and Ballmer have firmly denied the allegations. In a statement released to Torre, they said: "Neither Mr Ballmer nor the Clippers circumvented the salary cap or engaged in any misconduct related to Aspiration. Any contrary assertion is provably false."

This is not the first time investigators have examined Leonard's compensation with the Clippers. The NBA previously investigated Robertson in 2019 and determined at that time the team had not granted Leonard any impermissible benefits during the free agency period when he joined the club. The league indicated it would reopen that investigation if new evidence emerged.

Leonard, a six-time All-Star, signed with the Clippers in July 2019 after winning the NBA championship with the Toronto Raptors the previous season.

The NBA has not yet publicly commented on Torre's reporting. However, the league has established penalties for salary cap violations. Under the NBA collective bargaining agreement, the Clippers could face a fine of up to $4.5 million for a first offense if found to have attempted to circumvent the salary cap. The team could also lose a first-round draft pick as punishment.

The investigation represents a significant matter for the Clippers organization as the NBA examines whether the team engaged in competitive balance violations through improper compensation methods.

cards.headline: Knicks take 2-0 NBA Finals lead with road win over Spurs
cards.teaser: The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in Game 2 of the NBA Finals on Friday night, taking a commanding 2-0 series lead.
cards.body:
The New York Knicks defeated the San Antonio Spurs in Game 2 of the NBA Finals on Friday night, securing a 2-0 series lead. Karl-Anthony Towns led the Knicks' two-way effort, carrying the team on both offense and defense as New York held off a late Spurs rally. The victory marks just the third time in NBA Finals history that a team has won the first two games on the road.

A crucial mistake by Spurs star Victor Wembanyama in the final moments sealed San Antonio's defeat. The Knicks now head home with a commanding advantage, while the Spurs face the daunting task of climbing back from an 0-2 deficit in the championship series.

cards.headline: FIFA reverses World Cup water bottle ban after fan backlash
cards.teaser: The organization reversed its decision to prohibit refillable water bottles at tournament stadiums across North America following fierce criticism.
cards.body:
FIFA has reversed its decision to bar World Cup fans from bringing refillable water bottles into the tournament's 16 stadiums across North America. The reversal followed fierce backlash from fans and advocacy groups opposed to the original policy.

The ban would have forced fans to either purchase single-use bottles at stadiums or forgo water during matches. The environmental and practical concerns raised by the public outcry prompted FIFA to reconsider the restriction.

cards.headline: Aaron Judge reveals rib fracture originated from April diving catch
cards.teaser: The Yankees outfielder said the stress fracture in his right rib stems from diving for a ball in late April.
cards.body:
New York Yankees outfielder Aaron Judge has disclosed that his right rib stress fracture occurred during a diving play in late April. Judge attributed the injury to his effort to catch a ball during the defensive play.

The revelation clarifies the origin of an injury that has affected the star player throughout the season. What initially seemed like a minor incident from the diving attempt developed into a more significant problem for one of baseball's top performers.

cards.headline: NCAA denies Texas Tech appeal for quarterback Brendan Sorsby
cards.teaser: The organization rejected the school's request to reinstate the quarterback's eligibility.
cards.body:
The NCAA has denied Texas Tech's appeal to reinstate quarterback Brendan Sorsby's eligibility, according to multiple reports. The decision means Sorsby will remain ineligible to compete for the Red Raiders.

The ruling leaves Texas Tech without their quarterback as the program adjusts its roster plans moving forward.

cards.headline: SEC commissioner rejects talk of super league with Big Ten
cards.teaser: Greg Sankey called the notion that the conference wants to form a super league with the Big Ten not consistent with the truth.
cards.body:
SEC commissioner Greg Sankey has rejected speculation about a potential super league partnership with the Big Ten. He characterized such talk as "not consistent with the truth," pushing back against reports linking the two major conferences in discussions about a possible breakaway arrangement.

The comments address ongoing speculation about the future structure of college football as conferences continue to navigate significant changes.

cards.headline: Dana White says Pereira could surpass Jones as MMA's greatest with win over Gane
cards.teaser: The UFC president believes Alex Pereira would become the greatest fighter of all time if he defeats Ciryl Gane on June 14.
cards.body:
UFC president Dana White believes two-weight champion Alex Pereira will become the greatest MMA fighter of all time if he defeats Ciryl Gane on June 14 at the White House. White's statement underscores Pereira's elite status in the sport.

Pereira's potential victory over Gane would add another significant achievement to his resume as a multi-division champion, further solidifying his legacy in the UFC.

hero.headline: British Actor Anthony Head Dies at 72
hero.body:
Anthony Head, the British actor best known for playing Rupert Giles in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, has died at age 72. He passed away peacefully from complications related to pneumonia, surrounded by his family, according to a statement from his daughters Emily and Daisy Head.

"It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed first-hand the impact both he and his work have had on so many," they said.

Head achieved international recognition for his role as the mentor and librarian to Sarah Michelle Gellar's character in Buffy the Vampire Slayer, which ran for seven seasons. Beyond this iconic part, his career encompassed a wide range of television, film, and stage work. He appeared in the BBC fantasy series Merlin and played a recurring character in the sketch comedy show Little Britain alongside David Walliams and Matt Lucas. More recently, he joined the cast of Ted Lasso as Rupert Mannion, a former football club owner, where he developed strong on-screen chemistry with co-creator Jason Sudeikis.

His film roles included appearances in The Iron Lady and The Inbetweeners Movie. Before achieving fame through television, Head built a respected career on the stage, performing in West End productions including the original 1988 production of Chess, where he played Freddie Trumper. He also starred as Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1990 West End production of The Rocky Horror Show.

Born in Camden, London, Head came from an artistic family. His father founded Verity Films as a documentary filmmaker, while his mother was an actor who appeared in the 1960s BBC crime drama Maigret. His brother also worked as an actor. Head initially trained for a career in performance, beginning his professional work on stage before transitioning to screen roles.

In the early 1980s, Head also sang backing vocals for the British pop group Red Box and was featured on their 1986 debut album The Circle and the Square. He became well-known in the UK and US for his appearances in Nescafé Gold Blend television advertisements, which depicted a slow-developing romance between two neighbours.

Following the end of Buffy the Vampire Slayer in 2003, Head continued working steadily across various productions. During his time on Buffy, he lived in Los Angeles while his partner Sarah and two young daughters remained in England, travelling home every three or four weeks when possible.

Sarah Michelle Gellar paid tribute to Head through Instagram, beginning with a quote from her Buffy character before writing, "Well I don't have it figured out and I'm not ok. But I know I'm the lucky one because I knew you."

His daughters emphasized that his legacy would continue through the shows he appeared in and the audiences who loved them.

cards.headline: Actor James Handy Stabbed to Death in Los Angeles
cards.teaser: James Handy, a veteran actor who appeared in Top Gun: Maverick, was killed in a stabbing in Tarzana.
cards.body:
James Handy, an 81-year-old veteran character actor, was fatally stabbed at his home in Tarzana, Los Angeles on Wednesday morning. He was discovered unconscious in his front yard with multiple stab wounds to the chest and was pronounced dead at the hospital.

Michael Gledhill, 44, the son of Handy's girlfriend, was arrested and charged with murder in connection with the killing. Handy's film and television credits included roles in Top Gun: Maverick and Jumanji.

cards.headline: Shivani Pandya Malhotra Leaves Red Sea Film Festival
cards.teaser: The general manager who built Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Film Festival over five editions has stepped down.
cards.body:
Shivani Pandya Malhotra has resigned as general manager of the Red Sea Film Festival in Saudi Arabia. Malhotra played a central role in creating the festival and developing it into one of the most prominent film events in the Arab world over its five-year existence.

Under her leadership, the festival grew into the leading movie market in the Middle East and North Africa region. Malhotra oversaw the event's development from its inception, establishing it as a significant destination for filmmakers and industry professionals in a region where such festivals had limited presence before Saudi Arabia's recent cultural opening.

cards.headline: Sean Penn Skipped Oscars Ceremony for Mental Health Reasons
cards.teaser: The actor won Best Supporting Actor but did not attend to accept the award.
cards.body:
Sean Penn won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role in One Battle After Another but was not present at the ceremony to accept the statuette. Penn later stated he skipped the Oscars for mental health reasons.

The actor also discussed his dislike of selfies in the same interview. Penn's absence from the ceremony was notable given the significance of the award, one of the top honors in film acting. His decision to prioritize personal wellbeing over attending the high-profile event drew attention to ongoing conversations about mental health in the entertainment industry.

cards.headline: Taylor Swift Song for Toy Story 5 Breaks Streaming Records
cards.teaser: The singer's contribution to the upcoming Pixar film set multiple streaming records and received a music video.
cards.body:
Taylor Swift wrote a song titled "I Knew It, I Knew You" for Toy Story 5's cowgirl character Jessie. The track features a music video with footage of Joan Cusack's character and marks a return to the pop-country style that defined Swift's early career.

The Guardian's review praised the song as "full of handcrafted care and the rootsy soul of her country origins," calling it Swift's best work in years. Swift acknowledged the challenge of following Randy Newman's iconic Toy Story soundtrack work, describing Newman's contributions to the series as "incomparable."

cards.headline: Tattoo Artist Greg James Dies at 71
cards.teaser: The tattoo artist who worked with numerous rock musicians died at age 71.
cards.body:
Greg James, a tattoo artist known for his work with rock musicians, died at age 71. James built a reputation over decades as a preferred artist among performers in the rock music scene.

His clients included numerous well-known musicians who sought out his distinctive style and artistry. James became a recognized figure within both the tattoo and music industries through his long career serving high-profile clients in the entertainment world.

cards.headline: Elmo Draws Criticism from Knicks Fans Over NBA Finals Post
cards.teaser: The Sesame Street character faced backlash from New York basketball fans for not fully supporting the Knicks.
cards.body:
Elmo, the Sesame Street character whose fictional home is in New York, faced backlash from Knicks fans after taking a stance on the NBA Finals that fell short of fully supporting the city's basketball team. New Yorkers called the character a traitor for the perceived disloyalty during the championship series.

The incident underscored the passionate nature of sports fandom in New York, where even a beloved children's television character became the target of criticism for not wholeheartedly backing the local team.

hero.headline: Justice Department ends Trump anti-weaponization compensation fund
hero.body:
The Trump administration's nearly $1.8 billion anti-weaponization fund is effectively dead, according to a Justice Department filing submitted to federal court on Friday. The announcement marks the formal end of a controversial program that faced swift legal and political opposition since its announcement last month.

Two DOJ attorneys stated in their filing to the Eastern District of Virginia that the compensation fund "will not continue." The department made the statement while asking the court to reject legal challenges to the program, including a lawsuit filed by Democracy Forward.

The fund was created as part of a settlement in a Trump lawsuit against the Internal Revenue Service over the leak of his tax returns. The administration established it to compensate individuals who claimed they were targeted by federal investigations or prosecutions for political reasons. Officials indicated that potential recipients could include pardoned January 6 rioters.

The program faced immediate and intense backlash. US District Judge Leonie Brinkema in Virginia temporarily blocked the administration from transferring money from the fund last Friday, before the DOJ's announcement of its discontinuation.

Even Republicans expressed serious concerns about the initiative. Senate Majority Leader John Thune told reporters, "I do think the best way to handle it is if the administration decides to shut the fund down themselves." Mike Pence, Trump's first-term vice president, called the possibility of compensating January 6 rioters "deeply offensive" and said the concern was "broadly held by most Republicans and most Americans."

Democrats promised aggressive opposition. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called it "corruption in broad daylight" and a "$1.8bn Maga slush fund." He vowed that Democrats would force Senate Republicans to vote on measures to block payments and demand preserved records and hearings.

Several state governors proposed retaliatory measures. California's Gavin Newsom proposed a 100 percent income tax on any fund distributions to California residents. Similar proposals emerged from Illinois, New York, and Connecticut.

The fund drew criticism for its lack of transparency and oversight. The terms did not require disclosure of how much money would be paid to whom, raising concerns about potential misuse. Legal experts questioned the criteria for determining legitimate claims of political persecution versus standard law enforcement actions.

The compensation fund represented a signature Trump administration response to claims of political bias in federal law enforcement. Its termination suggests a shift in approach following the legal challenges and political pressure. The Justice Department has not announced any replacement program or alternative mechanism for addressing the concerns the fund was designed to address.

The Eastern District of Virginia has not yet ruled on the DOJ's request to dismiss the case, though the administration's statement that the fund will not continue likely moots the remaining legal claims for compensation under this specific program.

cards.headline: Whistleblower says DOGE plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead
cards.teaser: A whistleblower alleges that a proposed plan would have incorrectly designated millions of living people as deceased.
cards.body:
A whistleblower has come forward with allegations that a plan would have marked 2.7 million living people as dead in government records. The alleged plan was part of an immigration enforcement push, according to the whistleblower's claims.

The disclosure raises concerns about the accuracy of government data systems and the potential consequences for millions of people who could have been wrongly recorded as deceased. The whistleblower did not specify which agency or office within the government developed the plan or when it was proposed.

cards.headline: Trump acknowledges price increases for farmers at rally
cards.teaser: The president addressed higher costs facing farmers during remarks that also covered Washington infrastructure.
cards.body:
President Trump acknowledged that farmers are experiencing price increases during a rally where supporters voiced support for ending an unspecified war. The president specifically mentioned higher fertilizer and fuel prices affecting the agricultural sector.

Beyond agricultural issues, Trump devoted significant time to discussing Washington infrastructure, including the city's fountains and the Reflecting Pool. The remarks come as farmers face economic pressures from rising input costs that affect their profit margins and operational expenses.

cards.headline: Pete Sessions chief of staff charged with attempting to bring firearm into Capitol
cards.teaser: A top House staffer faces charges months after allegedly trying to bring a gun into the Capitol complex.
cards.body:
Luis Vega, chief of staff to Rep. Pete Sessions, was charged with two firearm-related counts in connection with an alleged incident last December. The charges were filed on Wednesday and relate to an alleged attempt to bring a firearm into the U.S. Capitol complex.

The alleged incident occurred days before Christmas. Vega serves as the top staffer for Sessions, a Texas Republican. The charges come several months after the incident allegedly took place in the Capitol complex, where firearms are prohibited except for authorized law enforcement personnel.

cards.headline: USDA confirms second screwworm case in Texas
cards.teaser: The Agriculture Department confirmed a second detection of the flesh-eating parasite as officials work to contain the outbreak.
cards.body:
The U.S. Department of Agriculture confirmed a second case of New World screwworm in Texas, detected in a one-month-old calf in Zavala County. The discovery prompted Texas to declare a state of disaster over the outbreak.

Canada responded by banning cattle imports from Texas as the U.S. races to contain and eradicate the flesh-eating parasite. Screwworm flies lay eggs in open wounds on livestock, and the hatched larvae feed on living tissue, potentially killing animals if untreated. The parasite was previously eradicated from the United States but remains a recurring threat.

cards.headline: New York passes bills regulating data centers and digital stalking
cards.teaser: The state legislature approved three bills covering data centers, surveillance pricing, and digital stalking protections.
cards.body:
The New York State Senate and Assembly passed three bills regulating data centers, surveillance pricing, and digital stalking. Governor Kathy Hochul will now decide whether to sign the measures into law.

The legislature did not advance other proposed measures covering environmental issues, housing, and entertainment that had been under consideration. The three bills that did pass represent efforts to address technology-related consumer protections and infrastructure regulation in the state.

cards.headline: Former CIA officer accused of gold theft must remain in jail
cards.teaser: A judge denied release for a former CIA officer facing charges of stealing gold bars.
cards.body:
A judge ruled that Rush, a former CIA officer accused of stealing gold bars, must remain in jail while the case proceeds. The judge told defense attorneys they can request another hearing if new evidence supporting release emerges.

The decision keeps the defendant in custody during the legal proceedings. The judge's order leaves open the possibility of reconsideration if the defense can present additional evidence that would justify pretrial release.
